newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 10.

text.p: The following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

The financial problems faced by constructors working with Japenese firms to build a bridge between the east Java city of Surabaya and the island of Madura are not related to recent controversy over Indonesia's national car policy, Public Works Minister Radinal Moochtar said. Japan recently took Indonesia to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over the Timor national car which is given preferential tax and tariff concessions.
Ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri was present at Jakarta's Central Court on Wednesday to support 64 of her supporters charged with taking parts in riots in the city in July.
The Indonesian Parliament has said that a bill to ban the use of, and trade in the designer drug Ecstasy is likely to come into effect early next year.
Chairman of the Capital Market Supervisory Agency (Bapepam), I Putu Gede Ary Suta, said on Wednesday that Indonesian security houses should set up an internal system to monitor unprofessional brokers

Dutch police have stressed that no member of the Indonesian Embassy in The Hague has been charged with forming part of an Ecstasy smuggling ring. The rumours, reported by Dutch tabloid De Telegraaf, are unrelated to the arrest last month of an Indonesian pilot found with 8,000 Ecstasy pills strapped to his waist, they said.
